1) cell therapy improves the function of the infarcted heart, 2) the beneficial effects are similar for BMNC and MSC, 3) captopril treatment improves the effect of both MSC and BMNC cell therapy, and 4) captopril has no beneficial effect on the infarct heart when administered alone.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel therapeutic approaches to the treatment of cardiovascular diseases.

the development and evaluation of new therapeutic strategies for the treatment of heart failure, in particular with the use of cell therapy and the combination of cell therapy with pharmacological treatment.

the beneficial effect of cellular cardiomyoplasty can be enhanced by captopril treatment.
cell therapy in combination with captopril treatment has a beneficial effect on cardiac function in a large myocardial infraction model.

the beneficial effect of MSC and BMNC therapy in large infarctions can be enhanced by captopril treatment, but the effect of the ACE‐inhibitors on cell survival, engraftment and differentiation is not clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of MSC and captopril treatment resulted in the best improvement of cardiac performance in the rat infarcted heart.
captopril therapy can enhance cell therapy in large infarctions.
the beneficial effect of cellular cardiomyoplasty can be improved by ACE‐inhibition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cell therapy can be effective in large infarctions and captopril treatment can enhance its effect.
the use of captopril in combination with cell therapy can improve cardiac function in large myocardial injury, which is not seen with captopril alone.
captopril does not enhance the effect of cell therapy on cardiac function in the infarcted heart.
